angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 653,958 km at 101.13 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.8885 +/- 0.0116 mas (same row, RUWE 0.95): 101.13 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.94 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 653,958 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.99 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5534 +/- 100 K from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2260.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.487, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2260 (pscomppars): spectral type G V, from Giacalone et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2260 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.22 dex, from Giacalone et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2260 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.19851, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2260 (pscomppars): age 0.321 Gyr, from Giacalone et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2260 (pscomppars): rotation period 8.45 d, from Giacalone et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/AJ/167/189/fig12 (Rotation period for 10909 TESS targets), column Prot: 8.58 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, TOI-2260: projected rotation speed 5.05 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2022AJ....163...99G)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.94 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.897. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
